bear_case: Counter-argument: a one-session bounce off a regime-trigger flush rarely marks the actual end of the move. Historically, equity drawdowns after a four-trigger breach (VIX, 30Y, breadth, sector dispersion all firing the same day) average 4-6 sessions to find the low and another 5-10 sessions to retest it. Monday's bounce off 7,318 is the textbook *first relief leg* that gets sold into within 2-3 sessions. The 30Y at 5.08% is still above the 5.0% trigger; until it closes below 5.0% for two consecutive sessions, the regime signal is intact, not resolved. Upgrading to HOLD this early risks adding back exposure just before the retest leg. Invalidation level: if SPX breaks back below 7,360 with VIX printing 19+ this week, the HOLD downgrade was premature and Step Aside should be reinstated.
